# The genes and tissues

Sixteen cytoskeleton genes from the lectures, and eight adult tissues from the
GTEx project.

```{r genes}
genes <- c("KRT5", "KRT14", "KRT8", "KRT18",    # keratins (epithelia)
           "VIM", "DES", "GFAP", "NEFL", "LMNA", # other intermediate filaments
           "MYH6", "MYH7", "MYH2", "MYH9",       # myosin II heavy chains
           "TUBB", "TUBB3", "TUBB4A")            # beta-tubulins

tissues <- c(Skin_Not_Sun_Exposed_Suprapubic = "Skin",
             Esophagus_Mucosa                = "Oesophagus mucosa",
             Liver                           = "Liver",
             Lung                            = "Lung",
             Muscle_Skeletal                 = "Skeletal muscle",
             Heart_Left_Ventricle            = "Heart (left ventricle)",
             Brain_Cortex                    = "Brain cortex",
             Nerve_Tibial                    = "Tibial nerve")
```

# Fetch expression from GTEx

This chunk is given. For each gene it asks the GTEx API for the gene's GENCODE
ID, then for the median expression (TPM) in every tissue, and keeps our eight
tissues. With `use_snapshot <- TRUE` it reads the course's saved copy instead.

```{r fetch}
retrieved <- "not yet"   # a default, so the text at the end always knits

if (use_snapshot) {
  snapshot_file <- "data/gtex-expression-2026-11-18.csv"
  if (!file.exists(snapshot_file)) {
    snapshot_file <- paste0("https://henriksson-lab.github.io/course_cellbiology/",
                            "bioinfo-cytoskeleton/data/gtex-expression-2026-11-18.csv")
  }
  expression <- read.csv(snapshot_file)
  retrieved <- "2026-11-18 (course snapshot)"
} else {
  gtex_api <- "https://gtexportal.org/api/v2/"
  rows <- list()
  for (gene in genes) {
    ref <- fromJSON(paste0(gtex_api, "reference/gene?geneId=", gene,
                           "&datasetId=gtex_v8"))$data
    gencode_id <- ref$gencodeId[ref$geneSymbol == gene]
    med <- fromJSON(paste0(gtex_api, "expression/medianGeneExpression?gencodeId=",
                           gencode_id, "&datasetId=gtex_v8&itemsPerPage=250"))$data
    med <- med[med$tissueSiteDetailId %in% names(tissues), ]
    rows[[gene]] <- data.frame(gene = gene, gencode_id = gencode_id,
                               tissue = med$tissueSiteDetailId, tpm = med$median,
                               dataset = "gtex_v8")
  }
  expression <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  retrieved <- as.character(Sys.Date())
}

# Cleaning: keep our genes, use readable tissue names, and fix the order of
# rows and columns so that related genes and tissues sit next to each other.
expression <- expression[expression$gene %in% genes, ]
expression$tissue <- factor(tissues[expression$tissue], levels = tissues)
expression$gene <- factor(expression$gene, levels = rev(genes))
rownames(expression) <- NULL
nrow(expression)   # 16 genes x 8 tissues = 128
```

# Example: a heatmap of raw TPM

This chunk is given. A heatmap draws one coloured tile (`geom_tile()`) per
gene and tissue. Here the colour is the raw TPM.

```{r example-heatmap, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(expression, aes(x = tissue, y = gene, fill = tpm)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "TPM") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Raw TPM") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# The three highest values, to check what you see:
head(expression[order(-expression$tpm), c("gene", "tissue", "tpm")], 3)
```

# Your heatmap: log scale

Copy the idea of the example, but colour by `log10(tpm + 1)`. The log makes a
gene at 10 TPM visible next to one at 10 000 TPM; the `+ 1` avoids `log10(0)`.

- **Blank 1:** the fill: `log10(tpm + 1)`.
- **Blank 2:** the layer that draws the tiles (see the example).
- **Blank 3:** the title of the colour key: `log10(TPM + 1)`.

```{r log-heatmap, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(expression, aes(x = tissue, y = gene, fill = ___)) +
  ___ +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "___") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "log10(TPM + 1)",
       caption = paste("Data: GTEx v8 median TPM, retrieved", retrieved)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
